name: Bolsonarism
summary: Bolsonarism is the Brazilian far-right movement built around Jair Bolsonaro. Scholars see it as a convergence of reactionary culture politics, militarism and ultraliberalism, with a personality cult around its leader and an openly sceptical stance toward the separation of powers. Its 2018 programme combined privatisation, pension capitalisation, deregulation and fiscal austerity with tough-on-crime measures, easier gun carrying and hostility to the left, land occupations and environmental enforcement.
scope: Bolsonarism as the Brazilian far-right movement named after Jair Bolsonaro, from his 2018 campaign through his presidency (2019-2022) and its aftermath, as scholarship describes it: a convergence of reactionary culture politics, militarism and ultraliberalism (Araujo and Carvalho), debated as authoritarian right-wing populism or neofascism (Resende's review of Boito and others), whose legacy outlasts Bolsonaro himself (Chirio). Follows the mainstream Bolsonarista core, not the Olavo de Carvalho ideological fringe; the 2018 government plan (InfoMoney report) is used only for its account of the programme.
